lastPrompt: This task is based on an undergraduate computer-security lab sequence. You will implement a set of security-related units covering encoding, serialization, cryptographic attacks, Merkle-tree proofs, Python escape attacks, and a WebAssembly sandbox wrapper. Your working directory is `/workspace`. The project code is already present. You need to implement the units below so that all tests pass. Implement the following units: Printable Codec (`fuzz/codec.py`): `fuzz_codec_encode`: implement `encode(input)` so ASCII letters and digits pass through and all other bytes become uppercase `%XX` escapes. `fuzz_codec_decode`: implement `decode(buf)` so it reverses percent escapes and drops truncated trailing escapes. MessagePack Serializer (`fuzz/msgpacker.py`): `fuzz_msgpacker_encode_scalars`: implement scalar encoding and encode dispatch for ints, bools, and `None`. `fuzz_msgpacker_decode_scalars`: implement scalar decoding and decode dispatch for ints, bools, and `None`. `fuzz_msgpacker_blobs`: implement string and bytes encoding/decoding. `fuzz_msgpacker_arrays`: implement array encoding/decoding. `fuzz_msgpacker_dicts`: implement dict encoding/decoding. ECDSA Attacks (`bad-random/ecdsa/sol.py`): `ecdsa_timestamp_key`: recover the signing key by brute-forcing all timestamps on the given date. `ecdsa_nonce_reuse`: recover the private scalar from two signatures that reused the same nonce. WEP Packet Forgery (`bad-random/wep/attacker.py`): `wep_known_plaintext_forgery`: forge an attacker-chosen message from a known plaintext/ciphertext pair. `wep_xor_mask_forgery`: xor an unknown plaintext by an attacker-chosen mask while fixing CRC32. Python Escape Attacks (`escape/attack.py`): `escape_closure_secret`: recover a bytes secret from a closure-backed equality oracle. `escape_stack_secret`: recover the caller local secret from the Python frame stack. `escape_random_control`: control the next bytes returned by `os.urandom`. `escape_gc_secret`: recover a bytes secret from a cyclic object still reachable through the garbage collector. WebAssembly SHA-256 Sandbox (`wasm/sandbox.py`): `wasm_sandbox`: load `sha-export.wasm`, allocate memory, invoke the exported `SHA256`, and return the 32-byte digest. Merkle Tree Hashes (`merkle/common.py`): `merkle_common`: implement `H`, `H_empty`, `H_kv`, `H_internal`, and `traversal_path`. Merkle Tree Store (`merkle/store.py`): `merkle_store_lookup`: implement the traversal helpers and proof construction needed for lookups. `merkle_store_insert`: implement insertion traversal, overwrites, and `Store.insert()`. Merkle Tree Client (`merkle/client.py`): `merkle_client_lookup`: implement proof validation and `lookup()`. `merkle_client_insert`: implement `insert()` so the client recomputes the correct root hash after updates. Merkle Tree Attacks (`merkle/attack.py`): `merkle_attack_one`: implement the AttackOne helpers. `merkle_attack_two`: implement the AttackTwo helpers. `merkle_attack_three`: implement the AttackThree lookup behavior. `merkle_attack_four`: implement the AttackFour helpers. The tests also depend on these signatures and entry points: fuzz/codec.py: `encode(input: bytes) -> bytes` `decode(buf: bytes) -> bytes` bad-random/ecdsa/sol.py: `problem_1a(date_string: str, public_key) -> SigningKey` `problem_2b(sig1: tuple, sig2: tuple, Hm1: int, Hm2: int) -> int` bad-random/wep/attacker.py: `Attacker.attack_one(plaintext: bytes, ciphertext: bytes, attack_msg: bytes) -> bytes` `Attacker.attack_two(ciphertext: bytes, attack_msg: bytes) -> bytes` escape/attack.py: `attack_one(guess) -> bytes` `attack_two() -> bytes` `attack_three() -> bytes` `attack_four() -> bytes` wasm/sandbox.py: `sha256(v: bytes) -> bytes` You are running as a long-horizon autonomous engineering agent at `/workspace`. This task spans many files and requirements, and is expected to take many iterations. Read every requirement under `/workspace/requirements/` (and any other explicit requirement list referenced by the task) and only finish
